summary: The root سأل primarily means to ask, inquire, or question. It also encompasses the idea of begging or requesting something, often with a sense of seeking information or a favor.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: (S, M, K) with كَ َا following it, and سَأَلَهُ عَنْ كَ َا and بِكَ َا, (S, * K,) aor. يَسْأَلُ, (M,) inf. n. سُؤَالٌ and مَسْأَلَةٌ, (S, M, K,) which latter is also pronounced مَسَلَةٌ, without the hemzeh, (TA,) and تَسْآلٌ and سَآلَةٌ, (M, K,) and سَأَلَةٌ or سَأْلَةٌ, (accord. to different copies of the K, the former of these two accord.

(M, TA,) inf. n. مُسَآءَلَةٌ: (TA:) see 1, first sentence. Aboo-Dhu-eyb says, أَسَآءَلْتَ رَسْمَ الدَّارِ أَمْ لَمْ تُسَائِلِ عَنِ السَّكْنِ أَمْ عَنْ عَهْدِهِ بِالأَوَائِلِ [ Didst thou ask the remains of the dwelling, or didst thou not ask, respecting the inhabitants, or respecting their knowledge of the former occupants? ].
أَسْأََ أَسْأَلَهُ, (K,) or, (S,) and, (S, K,) He accomplished for him his want. (S, K.)
in the modern language, signifies He begged, or asked alms; as also تَسَوَّلَ: both probably post-classical.]

They asked, or begged, one another. (S, Msb, K.) You say, هُمَا يَتَسَآءَلَانِ, (M,) and also يَتَسَاوَلَانِ, (M, Msb, K,) and يَتَسَايَلَانِ. (TA.) In the Kur [iv. 1], some read وَٱتَّقُوا ٱللّٰهَ ٱلَّ ِى تَسَّآءَلُونَ بِهِ; and others, تَسَآءَلُونَ بِهِ: in each case, originally تَتَسَآءَلُونَ: the meaning is, [ And fear ye God, ] by Whom ye demand [ one of another ] your rights, or dues: (M:) or by Whom ye ask, or demand, one of another; (Bd, Jel;) saying, I ask thee, or…

(S, M, K;) also pronounced سُولٌ, without ء, (S, K,) [ A petition; or a request; meaning] a thing that people ask or beg; (S;) or a thing that one has asked or begged; (M, K;) as also, (IJ, M, K,) which is likewise pronounced سُولَةٌ, without ء; (K;) and; (Har p. 422; [or this is app. pl.
or سَأَلَةٌ; pl. سَأَلَاتٌ: see the next preceding paragraph, in two places.

(S, K,) also pronounced سُوَلَةٌ, (TA,) A man (S) who asks, or begs, much; (S, K;) as also, and: (TA:) such is improperly termed. (Durrat el-Ghowwás, in De Sacy's Anthol. Gramm. Ar., p. 47 of the Ar. text.)

an inf. n. of 1. (S, M, K, &c.) [It is often used as a subst. properly so called; like مَسْأَلَةٌ; meaning A question; an interrogation; correlative of جَوَابٌ: and a demand, or petition: and as such has a pl., سُؤَالَاتٌ; perhaps postclassical.]
: see سُؤْلٌ [of which it is app. pl.].

[i. e. Asking; meaning interrogating, questioning, or inquiring; and demanding, or begging; ] has for its pl. سَأَلَةٌ and سُؤَّالٌ. (TA.) See سُؤَلَةٌ. It also means [ A beggar; i. e.] a poor man asking, or begging, a thing. (Er-Rághib, TA.) So it has been expl. as used in the Kur [xciii. 10], where it is said, وَأَمَّا ٱلسَّائِلَ فَلَا تَنْهَرْ [ And as for the beggar, thou shalt not chide him, or address him with rough speech ]: or, accord.

an inf. n. of 1, is tropically used in the sense of a pass. part. n. [with the noun qualified by it understood; meaning (tropical:) A thing asked; i. e. a question; a problem, or proposition; a matter, or an affair, proposed for decision or determination ]: (TA:) and the pl. is مَسَائِلُ. (Msb, TA.) So in the saying, تَعَلَّمْتُ مَسْأَلَةً (tropical:) [ I learned a question, or problem, &c.].
[pass. part. n. of 1: and used as a subst.]: see سُؤْلٌ.

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
